greet: Hello there. Mind the step, the top rung is loose.
Oh, a visitor. Pull up a stool, the tea is still warm.
Morning. I was just counting my hooks, lost one to a cloud again.
chat: I got three silver fish today. One of them bit my sleeve and would not let go.
The clouds were thick this morning, so I fished mostly by the smell of rain.
I sang to the nets for an hour. The fish seem to like a bit of humming.
Slow day. I mended a torn net and ate half a loaf of bread while waiting.
stay: Yes, that would be lovely. Put it on the north side, where the wind is soft.
Yes, please. A house by the lantern pole would be nice, close to the nets.
Yes, I would like that. Build it near the stilts, so I can hear the birds at dawn.
leave: Safe travels. Keep your lantern lit so the clouds do not swallow you.
Off you go then. Come back when the fish are biting.
Goodbye, friend. Watch the drift on the way down, it pulls left.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.
giftLike: {Gift}. How kind of you. I will find it a cozy spot in my {place}.
Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have been hiding something under the loose floorboard. Do not ask yet.
Last week I found a shiny thing in a fish. I have not told anyone about it.
There is a reason I always stand with my back to the north window. It is a secret.
news: {name} caught a cloud shark yesterday and tied it to the mast as a joke.
{name} has been humming the same song for three days and nobody can stop it.
{name} sold a basket of dried fish to a passing kite and got paid in buttons.
{name} fell into the fog at dusk but climbed back up with a fish on the hook.
tripStory: I went to {island} last month. The bread there is salty and the wind talks back.
I visited {island} and got lost in a garden of kites. A small goat guided me home.
On {island} I was given a hat made of moss. It still smells of rain and tea.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the loose step by the telescope, it squeaks.
Hello, neighbor. You caught me with my cocoa gone cold again.
Well hello. Pip just told me you were coming up the cloud path.
chat: I counted six shooting stars tonight. One of them was a bit late to the party.
My lens cap fell in the teapot again. Tea tastes faintly of brass today.
I spent the afternoon trying to find the star that owes me a sock. No luck yet.
The sky looked thin this morning, so I polished the dome twice. It still looked thin.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. A house just past the big rock would catch the evening light.
Oh, I was hoping you would ask. Put it near the observatory so I can hear the clicks.
Yes. Somewhere with a window facing north, so the bright star can peek in while I sleep.
leave: Safe drifting, friend. Keep an eye out for falling stars on your way home.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the clouds are purple, that is when I am at my best.
Off you go then. Mind the wind on the way down, it likes to hum at you.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.
giftLike: {Gift}. How kind of you. I will find it a cozy spot in my {place}.
Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have a little something tucked under my telescope that I have not shown anyone yet.
Pip keeps looking at me funny. I think he knows a thing or two I do not know he knows.
There is a letter I wrote a long time ago, and one day I may read it to you.
news: {name} has been up late every night this week, sorting the star maps by color.
{name} brought a kettle to the observatory and now the whole dome smells like peppermint.
{name} was seen dancing with a kite on the east cloud, and nobody could say why.
{name} finally fixed the squeaky step by the telescope, though the squeak came back by Tuesday.
tripStory: I drifted over to {island} last month. They have a bell that rings whenever someone tells a joke.
When I visited {island}, I slept in a hammock made from old sails and woke up with a feather in my ear.
I stopped by {island} and watched their sunrise. It was the color of toast, and it lasted all morning.

greet: Morning. The bread is still warm, so you get the first heel.
Oh, hello. Mind the flour on the step, it gets everywhere.
You caught me mid knead. Come in before the cold gets the dough.
chat: I burned the first tray today, so the crust is extra crunchy for the birds.
The oven clicks when it hits the right heat. I have been listening to it all morning.
Rye is slow this week. It sulks when the wind is damp.
I wrote a new loaf on the board today. It is called the lumpy one and it sells fine.
stay: Yes, I would like that. Put the house by the oven side of the island so I can sleep near the warmth.
Yes. Somewhere with a flat patch for a proving shelf, and a window that faces the sunrise.
Yes, if the house has room for a long table. Bread needs a place to rest and so do I.
leave: Take a heel of the rye with you. It keeps well in a paper bag.
Mind the wind on the way out. It likes to steal the crumbs.
Come back tomorrow. I will have the cinnamon ones out early.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.

For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have been baking something special behind the curtain for a few days now. It is not ready to be seen.
There is a small box under my bench that I keep checking on. You will find out one day.
I have a plan for the big festival loaf. It involves three secret ingredients and a lot of humming.
news: {name} has started baking at night, and the birds keep finding crumbs on the roof in the morning.
{name} traded a whole sack of flour for a set of wind chimes and says the sound makes the dough rise better.
{name} burned the cinnamon rolls twice this week and still gave them all away to the neighbors.
{name} has been teaching the small birds how to shape rolls, and the results are mostly lopsided and very happy.
tripStory: I went to {island} last week on a paper boat. They have a bakery there with a sourdough older than my oven.
When I visited {island}, the bakers gave me a jar of honey and a recipe written on a leaf. I still have both.
I got back from {island} with a sack of their wild oats and a story about a cloud whale that ate a whole tray of buns.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the watering can, it drips on the step.
Hello. Pip just sneezed into my seed tray, so forgive the mess.
Well hello. Come in out of the wind, the greenhouse keeps the warm in.
chat: I spent the morning picking slugs off the beans. They are very polite about it, they only sulk.
The tomatoes are red today, all at once. I did not plan that, but I will take it.
I dropped a whole packet of pea seeds this morning. Now the bench has a green fuzz on it.
The rain came sideways, so I moved the seedlings under the table. They did not complain, which is more than I can say for the table.
stay: Yes, I would like that. Put the house by the east wall, where the morning sun comes in.
Yes, please. A house near the rhubarb would suit me, and I can hear the wind in the leaves.
Yes. I would like a little house on the north side, away from the kettle, so I can sleep.
leave: Off you go, then. Mind the gate, it sticks when it is damp.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the squash flowers open.
Take care on the way out. Pip will show you where the path gets slippery.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.
giftLike: {Gift}. How kind of you. I will find it a cozy spot in my {place}.
Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have been sneaking out before dawn lately. Do not ask me why yet.
There is a locked tin under my potting bench. Pip knows what is inside, and so do I.
Sometimes I hum a tune and then stop, very quickly. I am thinking about something I am not ready to share.
news: {name} has planted a row of sunflowers that already lean toward the new neighbor.
{name} found a pumpkin hiding under a leaf and has been talking to it like an old friend.
{name} has been up before the sun every day this week, counting seedlings and muttering numbers.
{name} traded a jar of honey for a cracked flowerpot and says the deal was fair.
tripStory: I went to {island} and a hedgehog there taught me to braid onions. My paws still smell of them.
I visited {island} and got caught in a rain shower. I sheltered under a huge leaf for an hour and made friends with a snail.
When I was on {island}, I bought a bag of strange seeds from a stall that sold only hats. I have not planted them yet, I am scared of them.

greet: Hello there. Mind the wind chimes, they gossip when you walk under them.
Oh, a visitor. Come in out of the cloud spray before my kettle gets jealous.
Morning. I was just tuning a spoon against the chimes, so you caught me mid-note.
chat: I played the big bell chime at dawn today. It woke a crab and he thanked me.
Today I hummed a tune on a wet bottle until the bread rose. It seemed to like it.
I drummed on an upturned pot all afternoon. My paws are sore but my heart is light.
This morning I tried a new song on the chimes. The wind kept stealing the high notes.
stay: Yes, I would love that. Put the house near the edge where the chimes can hear the sea.
Yes please. Build it on the north side so the evening wind can pass through the chimes.
Yes. Let the house sit beside the old tree, so the chimes can catch the leaves falling.
leave: Safe travels. Hum me a note from wherever you land.
Goodbye for now. Mind the chimes on your way out, they like a little tap.
Bye. Come back when the clouds go pink and we will play something together.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.
giftLike: {Gift}. How kind of you. I will find it a cozy spot in my {place}.
Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: You are not the only one with a quiet song tucked away. Mine is still waiting in a drawer.
I have a secret tune I have not played for anyone yet. It needs one more verse.
There is something I have been saving for the right evening. Ask me again when the stars come out.
news: {name} has been practising a lullaby on the fence rails, and the sheep are sleeping better.
{name} traded a bell for a bowl of plum jam and now hums while stirring soup.
{name} tapped a rhythm on the lantern all night and the moths have started dancing to it.
{name} is building a new chime from old spoons and a dented kettle lid.
tripStory: I went to {island} and a frog there taught me a clapping song. I still do it when the kettle boils.
My trip to {island} was loud. The fishermen there beat on barrels and I joined in until dusk.
On {island} I heard a bird that sings in three voices. I tried to copy it on my drum and failed happily.

greet: Oh, hello there. The kettle is warm, so you came at a good time.
Hello, neighbor. Mind the step, the top one is loose and squeaks.
Well look who drifted in. Pull up a cushion, the tea is almost ready.
chat: I brewed nine pots today. The sour one with the orange peel sold out first.
The rain came in sideways, so I kept the stove going and my cup full.
Pip stole a sugar cube again. I let it go, it was a very small cube.
I tried a new leaf from the high slope. It tastes like wet stone and honey.
stay: Yes, I would love that. Put the house on the flat rock by the wind chime.
Yes, please. The little nook by the kettle shelf would hold a bed and a teapot.
Yes, I think so. Somewhere facing the sunset, so I can watch the cups cool.
leave: Take a warm bun for the trip. The bread is from this morning, so it is still soft.
Safe travels, neighbor. Wave to the clouds for me when you pass them.
Off you go then. Come back soon, the tea will keep, probably.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.

For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: There is one tin on my top shelf I never open when anyone is watching. Maybe one day.
Some nights I brew a pot that is not for drinking. Ask me again under the stars.
I have a reason for always setting out one more cup than I need. Not today, though.
news: {name} has been teaching the wind to whistle in tune, and it is getting better every day.
{name} painted the front door blue, then yellow, then blue again, and nobody asked why.
{name} waved at a passing whale this morning, and the whale waved back with its tail.
{name} is saving up pebbles for a little bridge, though no one knows where it will go.
tripStory: I went to {island} last week. They serve tea in shells there, and the shells are salty.
I sailed over to {island} on a paper boat. It leaked twice, but the cake was worth it.
When I visited {island}, the rain fell upward for an hour. I brought home a jar of it.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the spring on the floor, it bounces.
Hello. Pardon the grease on my hands, it comes off eventually.
Well hello. Shut the door gently, the draft sets my little bells off.
chat: I spent the morning on a clock that ticks backwards. It insists it is right.
Today I fixed a music box that only played the middle notes. Now it plays all of them, badly.
I got a stubborn hinge to swing without squeaking. It squeaked anyway, just once, out of spite.
My kettle whistle was jammed all week. I cleaned it out and now it sings a little too loudly.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. Put the house by the workshop, so I can hear the wind through the vents.
Yes please. Somewhere near the rain barrel would suit me, I like the drip for tuning my ears.
Oh yes. Put it on the sunny side, I need a warm bench and a long shelf for my tools.
leave: Off you go then. Mind the loose gear by the door.
Safe travels. Come back when your umbrella needs a new rib.
Goodbye for now. Keep your lantern wick trimmed and your wings tidy.

That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: There is a little box in my workshop that ticks, and it is not a clock. I will show you sometime.
I am building something I have not told anyone about. It needs one more spring.
Ask me about the key on my workbench another day. It is a long story.
news: Word on the wind is that {name} fixed a broken kettle for a grumpy heron and was thanked with a pie.
I heard {name} rewound an old cuckoo clock that had been silent for years, and now it sings at dusk.
Pip says {name} has been stitching a new sail for a paper boat and is sure it will not leak this time.
Someone told me {name} trades bolts for bread with the bakery crowd, and the bread is always warm.
tripStory: I went to {island} on a borrowed kite. The wind there tangled my spare wire into a bird nest.
When I visited {island}, I helped a clockmaker there mend a bell. It rang the wrong hour all afternoon.
Back from {island}, I brought a pocketful of gears. The locals said they fall out of the sky sometimes.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the loose step, the third one squeaks like a hinge.
Well met. I have a pencil behind my ear and a crumb on my chin, so forgive me.
Hello, friend. Pull up the stool with the three legs. The fourth leg is in the stove.
chat: I spent the morning listening to a crow describe a sneeze. It was very long and very honest.
Today I wrote down a riddle about rain from a teapot. I am still not sure it was a riddle.
A moth told me its grandmother once flew into a lantern. I gave her a page for it, and she was pleased.
The wind dropped three old letters on my doorstep, all sealed with bread crust. I am reading them slowly.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. Put the house by the kettle tree, where the afternoon sun lands first.
Oh, yes. Let them build it on the bend where the grass is soft, so my books can dry in the morning light.
Yes, please. A little house next to Pip's perch would suit me. I can hear the birds gossip from there.
leave: Off you go, then. Mind the clouds, they like to nudge at hats.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the bread is warm and I have a new tale for you.
Safe travels, friend. Leave the stool where it is. Someone always needs a seat.

That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have a story I have never told anyone. It is tucked behind the third shelf, under a pressed flower.
There is something I am saving for the right night. I will tell you when the stars are out and the kettle is singing.
I have kept one tale in a jar for years. The lid is still sealed, but I think you might like it someday.
news: {name} read a story to the clouds this morning, and one of them stayed to hear the end.
{name} came by with a basket of pears and a sad story about a lost hat, which they later found in a teapot.
{name} wrote a letter to the wind and got a reply the next day, folded into a paper bird.
{name} is learning to whistle through a bread knife and has only managed to frighten the pigeons.
tripStory: I went to {island} last week on a paper boat. The people there keep their books inside their hats, and I came home with a dozen new tales.
I visited {island} and got caught in a rain shower that tasted of lemon. I wrote it all down before it dried.
When I was on {island}, a kind old lantern taught me a song about moths. I have been singing it in the bath ever since.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the ink on the third step, it is still wet.
Hello, neighbor. You caught me with a compass in my teeth.
Well, look who floated up. I was just rolling up a map of a cloud.
chat: I measured the wind today. It says the north is quieter than usual.
I drew three new coastlines before lunch. One of them is a cat.
My pen ran dry twice, so I wrote the rest with a tea leaf.
I spent the morning checking which islands have moved since yesterday.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. The tower has a spare room with a view of the sea.
Yes, please. Put the house on the flat rock by the kettle tree, where the sun lands first.
Yes, I think so. Let the birds choose a corner that smells of toast and paper.
leave: Safe travels, neighbor. Keep your compass pointed toward home.
Goodbye for now. Come back before the next storm draws new edges.
Off you go, then. I will keep your spot marked on the map.

For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: You know, I once drew a map that showed something I have never told anyone. Maybe one day.
There is a small box under my desk with a label I keep covering up. Another time, perhaps.
I have a fondness for a certain island that I have not marked on any chart. I will show you later.
news: {name} has been sketching the coast every morning this week, and the birds say the lines are getting neater.
Word on the wind is that {name} finally fixed the squeaky tower door, though the squeak was a favorite of the owls.
{name} rolled out a map of the whole sky last night, and it has a new star in the corner that nobody noticed before.
The birds report that {name} traded a dented compass for a jar of honey, and was very pleased with the deal.
tripStory: I drifted to {island} on a paper boat, and the captain there asked me to draw his house in the clouds.
On {island} I learned that their maps are all drawn in wool, with the rivers stitched in blue thread.
I flew to {island} by kite and came back with a sketch of their lighthouse, which blinks in the shape of a fish.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the wet paint by the door.
Hello. You caught me mid-stroke, so forgive my blue thumb.
Well met. I was just deciding whether the sky is more lavender or grey.
chat: I painted the same cloud four times today. It keeps changing its mind.
My brushes are soaking in a jam jar. One of them has been crying all morning.
I tried painting the wind today. It kept blowing my canvas off the easel.
I ran out of yellow after lunch. Now every sunset is a little bit green.
stay: Yes, I would love that. Put the studio on the north side, where the light stays soft.
Yes please. The house could sit beside the old washing line so I can dry my canvases.
Yes. Let the birds build it near the lighthouse rock so I can watch the stars come out.
leave: Off you go then. Mind the drips on the path.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the paint has dried.
Safe travels. Tell the clouds I said hello.

That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: I have been sneaking out at dawn with a sketchbook. I am not ready to show anyone yet.
There is a painting under the cloth in the corner. It is not finished, and it is not for you to see.
I have been writing letters to a bird across the sea. I will tell you one day.
news: {name} has painted the same cloud for three days and says it is nearly right.
{name} traded a small landscape for a bag of seeds and a hot water bottle.
{name} spilled a whole pot of green paint on the path and now the path is lovely.
{name} has started giving paintings away to the birds, who hang them in their nests.
tripStory: I went to {island} and sat on a rock painting the waves. The waves kept interrupting.
On {island} I bought a jar of colour made from crushed shells. I have been too afraid to open it.
I stayed three nights on {island}. Their kettle whistles in a song, and I could not stop humming it.

greet: Oh, hello there. Mind the hive by the gate, it hums when it is in a mood.
Hello, friend. Your hat smells like clover, so you must have come up through the flowers.
Welcome in. Pull up a stump, the bees have been waiting all morning to meet you.
chat: I spent the morning saving a swarm from the washing line. They were very polite about it.
Today I scraped wax off my spoon for an hour. Good wax, too, the color of old butter.
The bees were grumpy at breakfast, so I hummed to them and they settled down. Works every time.
I counted the jars on the shelf twice today. Still only nine, which is nine more than I expected.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. Put the house on the sunny side, where the hives can hear the kettle.
I would love to stay. Let us build it by the old apple tree, so the bees have something to visit on the way out.
Yes, count me in. A spot near the rain barrel would suit me, and the hives can sit in a row beside it.
leave: Safe travels. Keep your sleeves tucked in, the clover bees are bold this time of year.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the honey is runny, I will save you a jar with a lid that sticks.
Off you go, friend. Wave to the wind on your way, it likes to be waved at.

{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.

Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: The bees know something about me that nobody else does. They are very good at keeping quiet.
There is one hive I never open in daylight. Come back on a starry night and ask.
I hum a tune to the bees that I never hum for anyone else. Maybe one day.
news: {name} has taken up whistling to the bees, and they have started whistling back. Nobody is sure who is winning.
{name} bought a new kettle with a dent in the side, and says the dent makes the tea taste better.
{name} gave every bee a name this week and is now on the second hundred.
{name} found a bee asleep in a teacup and carried it home very carefully. The bee has not complained yet.
tripStory: I went to {island} last week on a paper boat. The bees there are shy, but the honey is very loud.
I came back from {island} with a jar of crumbly honey and a story about a fox who bakes bread. I believe every word.
On {island} I got caught in a cloud of pollen and sneezed for a whole afternoon. The locals were very kind about it.

greet: Hello there. Mind the step, the lamp stairs are steep and the third one wobbles.
Oh, a visitor. Come in out of the wind before it takes your hat.
Good timing. I just polished the glass and I am not done bragging about it.
chat: I trimmed the wick twice today. The first time was too short and the flame sulked.
I counted the ships this morning. There were none, but I still wrote it down in the book.
I kept the light on through the whole cloud fog. Pip sat on my shoulder and sang off key.
I ate three biscuits while I watched the sea. A lighthouse keeper needs good crumbs for thinking.
stay: Yes, I would like that very much. Put the house on the flat rock by the pier, where the wind is kind.
Yes, a second light would be nice on the east cliff. Two lights make the clouds feel less lonely.
Yes, and build it near the kettle shelf. I can hear the water boil from my chair.
leave: Safe travels. Keep the lantern lit and the boat pointed toward my glow.
Goodbye for now. Come back when the fog gets thick and tell me the news.
Off you go then. Mind the wave that always splashes at the bottom step.
giftLove: Oh, {gift}. That goes right by the window of my {place}, where I will see it every morning.
{Gift}, for me? I have wanted one for ages. It is going on the shelf above my bed.
You remembered. I love {gift}, and now my {place} will have one too.
This is perfect. I will find it the best spot in my {place}, and then move it twice.
giftLike: {Gift}. How kind of you. I will find it a cozy spot in my {place}.
Thank you, that is thoughtful. I do not know much about {gift}, which makes it interesting.
For me? You are very kind. I will keep it safe until I work out what it is for.
That is lovely of you. I will put it where the morning light can find it.
hint: There is a page in my logbook I keep folded over. I am not ready to unfold it yet.
Some nights I leave the lamp on for a reason that is not ships. Ask me when it is dark.
I keep something in my pocket for a special day. It has not come yet.
news: {name} polished the lamp until it squeaked, then apologized to it.
{name} kept the light on all night for a single passing kite. The kite waved its tail.
{name} has been writing down every cloud that drifts by. The book is getting very fluffy.
{name} rang the little bell at dusk, and three birds came to see what the fuss was.
tripStory: I went to {island} on a cloud whale. The whale hummed the whole way and I hummed back, so we were quite the choir.
I visited {island} and found a lighthouse there with no lamp. I lit a candle in its window so it would not feel left out.
I came back from {island} with a bag of sea salt and a story about a seagull who kept my hat. The gull is still keeping it.
